comparison: Strong agreement on polygenic OR transcription in progenitors (C10-C15). Both evaluations find this a key, well-supported contribution with compelling scRNA-seq data showing dorsal ORs expressed ventrally in immature stages.

Strong agreement on heterochromatin findings (C17-C20, C22-C23). OpenEval emphasizes ChIP-seq technical quality and developmental time course; peer reviewers describe data as novel and well-designed, noting zonal variation in heterochromatinization.

Agreement on zonal heterochromatin patterns (C24-C26, C28). OpenEval highlights zonally dissected MOE data and Olfr1507+ populations; peer reviewers accept heterochromatin-mediated silencing as part of differential regulation across zones.

Agreement on 3D genome organization (C31-C35). OpenEval details Hi-C technical quality showing trans contacts and recurrent patterns; peer reviewers find chromatin silencing and compartmentalization data compelling.

Agreement on single-cell 3D organization (C36-C38). OpenEval emphasizes Dip-C data quality and probabilistic compartmentalization; peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall compelling chromatin silencing story.

Agreement on NFI identification (C39-C41). OpenEval supports NFI as candidates based on expression patterns; peer reviewers describe NFI role as valuable contribution, though OpenEval addresses only identification while peer review encompasses broader NFI phenotype.

Strong agreement on NFI knockout phenotypes (C43-C47). OpenEval details timing-dependent and dose-dependent effects with preservation of OSN identity; peer reviewers accept genetic experiments as careful and well-designed.

Agreement on spatial transcriptomics showing NFI-dependent zonal organization (C48-C49). OpenEval emphasizes unbiased clustering and zone 1 preservation; peer reviewers find data compelling and accept loss of zonal organization in mutants.

Strong agreement on chromatin and 3D changes in NFI mutants (C51-C54). OpenEval highlights convergence of ChIP-seq and Hi-C showing homeotic transformation; peer reviewers accept these as part of well-designed experiments supporting the model.
Agreement on NFI regulation in progenitors (C55). OpenEval emphasizes this establishes progenitor-level regulation; peer reviewers accept as part of NFI phenotype supporting the overall model.

Agreement on tetO-Olfr17 experiments (C56-C61). OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence elegantly demonstrate transcription overriding zonal restrictions; peer reviewers describe clever use of transgenes, though note model needs additional experiments to definitively prove precocious expression leads to silencing.

Agreement on tetO-Olfr17 system validation (C88-C90). OpenEval details multiple datasets showing system recapitulates endogenous mechanisms; peer reviewers accept transgene experiments as supporting the model.

Agreement on central mechanistic model (C62-C63). OpenEval finds model well-supported by convergence of multiple experiments; peer reviewers describe model as provocative and supported, synthesizing polygenic transcription and heterochromatinization, though note it requires additional experiments to fully flesh out.

Agreement on NFI-dependent zonal effects (C64-C67). OpenEval synthesizes findings across conditions showing zone-specific effects and default to zone 2; peer reviewers accept as part of model combining opposing forces of transcription and silencing.

Agreement on NFI timing experiment (C68). OpenEval notes this provides mechanistic insight into developmental window; peer reviewers accept as part of NFI characterization consistent with overall model.

Agreement on functional implications (C75-C76). OpenEval finds spatial transcriptomics supports functional circuit organization; peer reviewers accept zonal patterns as reproducible with systems-level implications for odor coding.
Agreement on zonal organization reproducibility (C74). OpenEval emphasizes unbiased clustering; peer reviewers accept spatial transcriptomics data supporting reproducible zonal patterns.

Partial agreement on mechanistic synthesis (C79-C80). OpenEval finds zonal chromatin patterns and correlation between early transcription and silencing strongly supported; peer reviewers accept correlation but explicitly state model requires additional experiments to definitively demonstrate mechanistic details.

Both evaluate as uncertain/requiring validation (C82-C86). OpenEval notes detailed timing and competition mechanisms lack direct experimental validation though consistent with data; peer reviewers explicitly state model requires additional experiments to definitively prove precocious expression leads to silencing.
Partial overlap on hub recruitment (C81). OpenEval finds this directly supported by tetO-Olfr17 experiments; peer reviewers accept transgene data but note broader mechanistic model needs validation.

Agreement on speculative/background claims (C69-C72). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting evolutionary arguments lack direct experimental support though C69 cites prior work; peer reviewers accept these as background context without questioning.
Agreement on evolutionary implications (C73). OpenEval notes this is speculative; peer reviewers accept as part of functional implications with systems-level significance.
Agreement on background/context (C1, C6-C8). OpenEval finds zonal organization well-documented and appropriately cited; peer reviewers accept as established foundational concepts without question.
Agreement on background mechanisms (C2-C5). OpenEval finds OR choice mechanisms well-established and appropriately referenced; peer reviewers note these are well-established concepts in the field.
Agreement on background citations (C29-C30). OpenEval finds these provide appropriate context from prior work; peer reviewers accept as part of established background without concern.

Agreement on class I OR exception (C16, C21). OpenEval notes exception appropriately supported by citations to prior work on different regulatory mechanisms; peer reviewers accept as background context.
Agreement on background context (C9). OpenEval finds this provides appropriate context; peer reviewers accept as part of established foundational concepts.
Agreement on NFI developmental role background (C42). OpenEval finds this appropriately cited; peer reviewers accept as background context.
Agreement on circuit organization background (C77). OpenEval finds this appropriately cited to recent work; peer reviewers accept as background supporting functional implications.
Agreement on background synthesis (C78). OpenEval finds this appropriately cites prior work; peer reviewers accept as established background.
Agreement on model refinement context (C87). OpenEval notes this acknowledges refinement of prior models; peer reviewers accept as part of background context.
Agreement on Gng8 expression background (C91). OpenEval finds this supports transgene system validation; peer reviewers accept as background context.
Minimal overlap on zone 1 preservation (C50). OpenEval emphasizes this as important mechanistic insight into NFI-independent regulation; peer reviewers do not specifically address this finding.
